A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for any graph with a small separator, we can route along near-short path using O(log2 n) labels with logarithmic stack depth, and that for trees and planar graphs we can route using O(logk n) labels with stack depth of O(k logk n).
we give a trade-off between the number of labels and the stack depth for routing on trees, and show that this trade-off holds for other graphs as well.

we show how to achieve optimal tradeoffs between the number of labels, the maximum stack depth and the quality of the routing paths, in a variety of network topologies, including trees, planar and bounded-degree graphs.

the MPLS routing model is a very rich and powerful model for designing routing protocols for networks, and we are able to achieve results that were impossible to achieve in the conventional IP model, and which are very close to being optimal.
